The thesis in four sentences: Online AGMARKNET spreads tempt dispatchers, yet chasing top lagged spreads (B1_lagged_screen) across 58,676 test episodes loses money on 45.21% of dispatches (worst-10% ES10 −₹641.26/qtl, with 28.98% turning back sequentially). Earlier black-box trees, weather leaks, and tuned kappa* = 5.0 thresholds were audited and retired. Replacing them with zero-parameter Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 (weekday reporting probability × 1-SD safe spread exceeding sunk freight), settlement-matched Safe_EV_Phys_m0 (1.5F), and Class-8 RT_2F_Min_m0 lowers losses to 14.93% and strengthens ES10 to −₹344.09/qtl (+₹181.17 vs road baseline B2_age_matched, two-sided Holm p = 0.0024 at R = 5,000 across all 3 clusterings, 1/2/4-week blocks, strict 2024-only 171 markets, realized ERA5 settlement, and all 6 states). These rules act transparently as an upstream 6 a.m. alert filter ahead of live arhtiya phone confirmation while disclosing exact silent-market break-even (+₹328.37/qtl above turn-back; 23.79% Open-MAR share), Open-MAR mean bounds, 41.38% HP apple conditional losses, and blocked future Gate J.

Part 1: Problem, Epistemic Table 1, Data Provenance & Settlement Physics

1. Three Research Questions and Honest Methodological Scope

Indian wholesale agricultural markets (mandis) publish daily minimum, modal, and maximum prices by variety on AGMARKNET. While digital price dissemination can narrow spatial dispersion when market frictions are low [jensen2007digital, goyal2010information], empirical evidence across rural India and developing economies shows that raw price portals frequently fail to translate into realized arbitrage [fafchamps2012sms, courtois2015farmer, mitra2018asymmetric, chatterjee2023market]. Four operational mechanisms separate a screen spread from realized net gain:

  1. Decision-Time Reporting Lag: At 6 a.m. dispatch time t—when FPO managers decide whether to load a truck or suppress a portal alert—same-day auction prices have not cleared, and thinner yards publish intermittently (1..7 days late).
  2. Transfer Costs, Destination Statutory Fees, and Biological Decay: Road freight, single-lane hill terrain, out-of-district APMC seller fees levied on destination auction value, and ambient transit spoilage erode gross price gaps [baulch1997transfer, nabcons2022phl].
  3. Auction Volatility and Arrival Execution Risk: A single elevated lagged modal quote at a volatile market (dest_price_cv_28d) frequently reverts by arrival day t + τ, and an empty arrival board (settle_any_min_dw = NaN) indicates no recorded commodity trade in the public portal [deka2026missing].
  4. Role of Automated Triage vs Live Trader Confirmation: Farmers dispatching a 30-quintal load normally verify live yard activity through a 30-second phone call to a destination arhtiya (commission agent) [jensen2007digital, ziegler2019fresh]. Automated dispatch scoring operates strictly as an upstream 6 a.m. alert-triage filter helping FPO coordinators prioritize promising corridors and suppress noisy alerts before dialing traders, rather than replacing phone verification.

We address three research questions across six Indian states (Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh) and four crops (Onion, Potato, Tomato, Apple):

  • RQ1 (Screen-Chasing Loss Incidence and Settlement Realism): Under a strict <= t - 1 chronological firewall and non-anticipative sequential arrival settlement, how often do attractive lagged portal spreads (> ₹100/qtl) lose money, and how strongly do 3-day hindsight settlement and ex-post day-t origin conditioning distort observed risk?
  • RQ2 (Zero-Parameter Expected-Value Rules vs Equal-Age Baselines and Tuned Heuristics): On identical Top-5 candidate menus and equal quote ages (1..3 days), can threshold-free, zero-hyperparameter rules (Safe_EV_Sunk_m0, settlement-matched Safe_EV_Phys_m0, and Class-8 phone-calculator RT_2F_Min_m0) improve episode loss incidence and worst-10% ES10 over validation-tuned road rules (B2_age_matched), hard-gated heuristics (MG_matched), and our tuned reliability-weighted extension (RR_Abstain_matched, κ* = 5.0)?
  • RQ3 (Identification Bounds, Zero-Lookahead Panel, Realized ERA5 Weather, and Subgroup Generalizability): How stable are these gains across exact silent-market break-even thresholds and Manski/MAR missing-quote bounds [rubin1976inference, manski1990bounds], a fresh zero-lookahead 2024-only 171-market rebuild, realized ERA5 destination arrival-day weather settlement, 18 frozen and re-scored cost scenarios, exact-geocoded corridors, an 88,014-episode unconditional origin panel, all six states, every crop, and high-dispersion Himachal Pradesh graded apples?

Explicit Protocol Chronology (Stage I -> A10 -> A18 -> Revision v6)

  1. Stage I Legacy Baseline (e421d15): An unlagged gradient-boosted tree system (HistGradientBoostingRegressor) with ERA5 weather and conformal intervals proved inconclusive against same-day road dispatch B2 on confirmatory H2 (+₹6.13/qtl, 95% CI [−₹17.02, +₹25.02], Holm p = 0.2699) and failed on Himachal Pradesh graded apples. We preserve these negative findings intact.
  2. Audit Remediation (A10, Commit 87a0b62): Removed all day-t shortlist and origin price leaks, removed 98.64% ERA5-identical forecast weather from decisions, corrected APMC fee bases (M9), fixed exact fractional ES10 computation, and tested reliability-weighted RR-Abstain. Subsequent adversarial audit identified four weaknesses: a missing State| destination cluster-key prefix (336 split clusters instead of 172 physical yards), unlabeled one-sided p-values, hitting the validation grid ceiling at κ* = 5.0 (masking an implicit threshold shift), and incomplete subgroup/missingness robustness for RR.
  3. Zero-Parameter Simplification (PREREG_A18.md, Commit 4cbb02d) & Unified Revision v6 Audits: Keeping test outcomes quarantined during validation rule design (2025-01-01..2025-05-31), we committed closed-form zero-parameter rules before executing revision/eval_a18.py, and in Revision v6 (revision/eval_v6.py) added a strict 2024-only 171-market zero-lookahead check, realized ERA5 arrival-weather settlement (with zero weather in decisions), exact algebraically verified break-even silent-market thresholds, and R = 5,000 paired cluster bootstraps across 1-, 2-, and 4-week calendar blocks. Because calendar 2025-06-01..2026-04-08 and HP apples were observed in earlier repository commits, all post-Stage-I evaluations are labeled explicitly exploratory (exploratory: true) wrt prior calendar exposure.

2.4 Causal Timing Firewall and Counterfactual Property Tests

At morning decision time t, every input entering shortlisting or policy scoring predates day t (dest_quote_date < date, origin_quote_date < date). Realized settle_local_price_d0, arrival quotes settle_dest_modal_d0..d2, settle_any_min_d0..d2, and Section 4.4 realized ERA5 weather columns reside exclusively in the settlement namespace. Automated counterfactual tests in tests/test_timing_and_leakage_r3.py corrupt all prices on days ≥ t* (injecting ₹99,999/qtl spikes at excluded yards, halving day-t* local prices, and deleting active candidates on days ≥ t*) and assert bit-for-bit equality of the shortlisted candidate menu and every decision feature for t ≤ t*.

3. Payoff Physics, Sequential Settlement, and Decision Rules (With Numeric Examples)

3.1 Physical Freight, Statutory Destination Fee (M9), and Biological Spoilage

For corridor c = (o → d) in state s and commodity k:

Freightroad(c) = 35.0 + 0.45 · hs · road_km(c)

where hs = 1.45 in Himachal Pradesh (91.59% single-lane roads [hpeconsurvey2026]) and 1.0 elsewhere. Reference 20°C / 65% RH biological decay over transit truck_hours plus waiting days w ∈ {0, 1, 2} [kader2002postharvest, gross2016usda66] is:

s(k, w) = min(0.55, bk · max(1, truck_hours + 24 w)24)

with NABCONS 24-hour market-level rates bk ∈ {0.0325 Tomato, 0.0196 Onion, 0.0164 Apple, 0.0086 Potato} [nabcons2022phl]. In our Section 4.4 realized ERA5 settlement check, decay scales by ambient arrival-day Q10 = 2(Tmax-20)/10 and humidity factor 1 + 0.25 max(0, (RH-70)/30), while heavy arrival rain (rain >= 35 mm) adds +0.02 rot fraction and shifts realized exact-variety sale price halfway toward Min_Price. Statutory APMC seller fees τfee(c) ∈ {0, 0.005, 0.010, 0.015} (0 if same_district) apply strictly to post-spoilage destination gross sales, and equal 0 if the truck returns home unsold.

Worked Example 1 (Physical Freight, Spoilage & Destination-Base Statutory Fee): Consider an out-of-district Tomato trip in Madhya Pradesh (fee_rate = 1.5%, hs = 1.0) with road_km = 200 km, truck_hours = 6 hours, and immediate arrival sale (w = 0) at sale_price = ₹2,000/qtl, vs local settle_local_price_d0 = ₹1,500/qtl:

  1. Freight: F = 35.0 + 0.45 × 1.0 × 200 = ₹125.00/qtl.
  2. 20°C spoilage: s(0) = 0.0325 × (6 / 24) = 0.008125 (0.8125%).
  3. Post-spoilage gross auction revenue: ₹2,000 × (1 - 0.008125) = ₹1,983.75/qtl.
  4. Net after 1.5% statutory fee: ₹1,983.75 × 0.985 = ₹1,953.99/qtl.
  5. Modeled net dispatch gain: ₹1,953.99 - ₹125.00 - ₹1,500.00 = +₹328.99/qtl.

3.2 Sequential Non-Anticipative Settlement vs Hindsight Lookahead

Starting at w = 0 on arrival day tarr = t + τ (tau_days in 1..3), settlement advances day by day without future lookahead:

  • Sell exact: If exact-variety Modal_Price is reported on day w, sell: ΔNetsell(w) = Psale(1 - s(k, w))(1 - τfee) - F - 25 w - Ploc, d0.
  • Wait (w < 2): If exact variety is missing on day w while another variety of the crop trades (settle_any_min_dw > 0), wait 1 day (₹25/qtl-day detention + 24h decay).
  • Turn back / distress fallback: If no variety of the commodity is recorded on day w, divert home with zero APMC fee: ΔNetdivert(w) = -div· F - Ploc, d0· s(k, w) - 25 w (baseline div = 1.5; if day w = 2 still shows another variety, sell at 0.90 * settle_any_min_d2 after fee and ₹50 detention).

By contrast, 3-day hindsight settlement peeks ahead across d0..d2 even when arrival day 0 shows zero commodity trade.

Worked Example 2 (Sequential No-Lookahead vs 3-Day Hindsight): On our MP Tomato trip (F = ₹125, Ploc, d0 = ₹1,500), suppose destination Tomato is absent on arrival day 0 (settle_any_min_d0 = NaN), though exact-variety trades at ₹2,000 on day +1:

  • Sequential (realistic): Seeing an empty tomato auction on day 0, the truck diverts at w = 0 (zero fee): ΔNet = -1.5 × 125 - 1,500 × 0.008125 = -₹199.69/qtl.
  • 3-day hindsight: Clairvoyant waiting (w = 1, s(1) = 0.040625, detention ₹25) records +₹239.97/qtl—a ₹439.66/qtl hindsight distortion.

3.3 Equal-Menu Baselines, RR-Abstain, and Zero-Parameter Expected-Value Rules

Every rule evaluates the same Top-5 lagged menu (lag_spread > 100) and selects at most one corridor (else abstains with ΔNet = 0). All comparators share identical quote-age freshness (dest_lag_age in 1..3):

  1. B1_lagged_screen: Highest raw lag_spread across age 1..7 (100% dispatch).
  2. B2_age_matched: Road- and fee-adjusted net spread G(c, t) - Froad(c) > ₹200/qtl, where G = Pdest,lag(1 - τfee) - Porig,lag, tuned on validation (70.71% dispatch).
  3. B_simple_activity_matched & MG_matched: Adds 14-day reporting (rep14 >= 0.50) or dual hard gates (rep14 >= 0.50 & dow8 >= 0.35) plus 20°C spoilage, matched to validation 70.71% dispatch (m_mg_match = ₹131.26).
  4. Tuned RR_Abstain (A10, Commit 87a0b62): Mixes open-market payoff Δ̂open and a bounded loss -κ Froad - Porig,lag sref,0 weighted by p̂rep = 0.5 rep28 + 0.5 dow8. Limitation Identified by A17/A18: Validation optimization hit the grid ceiling κ* = 5.0 (3.33× physical diversion 1.5), compensating for two omissions: rep28 smoothed over Sunday closures, and RR ignored auction price volatility. Extending κ to 20.0 drives the matched cutoff down to −₹328.99/qtl (a10_summary.json), showing that κ = 5.0 acted as a tuned threshold shift rather than a parameter-free constant.

To remove κ tuning, rep28 Sunday smoothing, and biological spoilage lookups simultaneously, we locked three zero-hyperparameter closed-form rules (PREREG_A18.md, fixed S > 0):

  1. Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 (Primary Zero-Parameter Tail-Risk Rule): Combines arrival-weekday Laplace reporting frequency pdow = dest_dow_exact_rep_8w ∈ {110, …, 910} with a 1-standard-deviation conservative spread G1SD(c, t) = Pdest,lag(1 - cv28)(1 - τfee) - Porig,lag against sunk one-way freight Froad:
SSafe-EV(c, t) = pdow(c, t) · G1SD(c, t) - Froad(c) > 0   ⟺   G1SDFroad > 1pdow
  1. Safe_EV_Phys_m0 (Settlement-Matched 1.5F Variant, 0 Tuned Params): Applies the exact baseline diversion multiplier 1.5 directly inside the expected-value inequality with zero tuning:
SSafe-EV-Phys(c, t) = pdow(c, t) · (G1SD(c, t) - Froad(c)) - (1 - pdow(c, t)) · 1.5 Froad(c) > 0
  1. RT_2F_Min_m0 & RT_2F_Dow_m0 (Class-8 Phone-Calculator Rule, NO cv28, NO spoil): Using plain fee-adjusted spread G and pmin = min(rep28, pdow), dispatch iff expected revenue clears round-trip freight (2F):
SRT-2F-Min(c, t) = pmin(c, t) · G(c, t) - 2 Froad(c) > 0   ⟺   G2 Froad > 1pmin

Worked Example 3 (Zero-Parameter Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 and Class-8 RT_2F_Min_m0 in 10 Seconds): Take our MP Tomato route (Porig,lag = ₹1,500, Pdest,lag = ₹2,000, τfee = 1.5%, Froad = ₹125, cv28 = 0.15), giving G = 2,000(0.985) - 1,500 = +₹470.00/qtl and 1-SD safe spread G1SD = 2,000(0.85)(0.985) - 1,500 = +₹174.50/qtl.

  • Steady Yard A (dow8 = 0.90, rep28 = 0.85, so pmin = 0.85):
  • Safe_EV_Sunk: 0.90 × 174.50 - 125 = +₹32.05 > 0 ⟹ DISPATCH (Ratio 174.5/125 = 1.40 > 1/0.90 = 1.11).
  • RT_2F_Min (no volatility needed): 0.85 × 470.00 - 250 = +₹149.50 > 0 ⟹ DISPATCH.
  • Sunday / Thin Yard B (dow8 = 0.20, rep28 = 0.60, pmin = 0.20): Notice B2_age_matched scores Yard B +₹345 (+₹470 - ₹125) identically to Yard A and dispatches. Both zero-parameter rules abstain immediately: Safe_EV_Sunk: 0.20 × 174.50 - 125 = -₹90.10 < 0; RT_2F_Min: 0.20 × 470 - 250 = -₹156.00 < 0 ⟹ STAY HOME.

3.4 Exact Tail Shortfall (ES10) and Corrected Two-Way Cluster Inference (R = 5,000)

Following coherent Conditional Value-at-Risk / expected shortfall at α = 0.10 [rockafellar2000cvar] (revision/es10.py), we sort all n episode outcomes x(1) ≤ … ≤ x(n) (0 on abstention) with fractional tail mass m = 0.10 n = k + f (k = ⌊ m ⌋, f = m - k):

ES10(x) = 1m(∑i=1k x(i) + f · x(k+1))

Worked Example 4 (Exact Fractional ES10): On {1, 2, …, 11}, m = 1.1 (k = 1, f = 0.1), giving ES10 = (1 + 0.1 × 2)/1.1 = 1.2/1.1 ≈ 1.09, unlike unweighted below-quantile averaging (1.50).

After fixing a key-prefixing defect uncovered during review (bare dest_market previously lacked State| and split physical markets into 336 artificial clusters instead of 172), all primary inference uses paired two-way cluster bootstraps with multiplicative market-by-time resampling weights, percentile confidence intervals, Phipson–Smyth +1 two-sided finite-sample p-values [phipson2010permutation], and two-sided Holm–Bonferroni FWER control (p_holm_2s) [holm1979simple] (R = 2,000 in frozen a18_bootstrap.csv and R = 5,000 in v6_bootstrap_5000.csv, minimum two-sided p = 0.0004, 6-test Holm floor 0.0024) across:

  1. origin_x_2week: 173 origin State|Market clusters × 23 fortnights (plus 1-week [45 blocks] and 4-week [12 blocks] sensitivity in Section 4.4);
  2. b2dest_or_origin_x_2week: 172 State-prefixed B2 destination (or origin) clusters × 23 fortnights;
  3. policy_dest_or_origin_x_2week: 171–173 policy-specific chosen destination (or origin) clusters × 23 fortnights.

4. Results

4.1 RQ1: Screen-Chasing Loss Incidence and Arrival Outcomes

Across N = 58,676 test episodes, chasing the highest raw lagged spread above ₹100/qtl (B1_lagged_screen, 100.00% dispatch) loses money on 45.21% of episodes (mean ₹397.87/qtl, ES10 −₹641.26/qtl, Table 3). Outcome decomposition (a18_outcome_mix.csv) shows that 69.47% (40,765 trips) sell exact variety on arrival day 0, 0.49% wait 1–2 days to sell, 1.05% sell another variety on day 2, and 28.98% (17,005 trips) find zero recorded commodity trade on arrival (27.99% day 0, 0.64% day 1, 0.35% day 2) and incur the return branch. Scoring those identical B1 trips with 3-day hindsight lookahead depresses apparent loss incidence artificially from 45.21% to 31.35% (mean ₹538.96/qtl).

4.2 RQ2: Zero-Parameter Expected-Value Rules vs Baselines, Hard Gates, and Tuned RR-Abstain

Tables 3, 4, and 5 trace the gain achieved while removing complexity:

  1. Hard-Gated MG_matched Leaves Tail Risk Unchanged (p_holm_2s = 1.000): At matched ~70% dispatch, MG_matched raises mean payoff over B2_age_matched (+₹34.34/qtl, two-sided Holm p = 0.0120 origin / 0.0550 B2-dest) and lowers episode losses (−8.15 pp, p_holm_2s = 0.0120), but worst-10% ES10 does not improve (−₹512.78 vs −₹525.25, diff +₹12.48/qtl, CI [−₹16.57, +₹39.97], p_holm_2s = 1.000). Even tuning MG's hard gates directly for validation ES10 (rep28 >= 0.75, dow8 >= 0.35) reaches only ES10 −₹445.92 at a sharp mean reduction (₹358.44/qtl, a18_fair_ablations.csv).
  2. Tuned RR_Abstain Improves ES10, Yet Exhibits Grid-Ceiling Dependence and Higher Loss Severity: RR_Abstain_matched (k*=5.0) improves ES10 (−₹460.72: +₹64.54 vs B2_age_matched and +₹52.06 vs MG_matched, p_holm_2s = 0.0040 origin/B2-dest and 0.0060 RR-dest), yet hits the grid ceiling kappa = 5.0, incurs worse average loss severity when wrong (loss_given_loss −₹308.18 vs B1 −₹271.24 and B2 −₹293.73), and does not reach significance on its +₹7.46 mean difference vs MG_matched (p_2s = 0.241..0.477). Raising kappa to 20.0 reaches val ES10 −₹371.53 only by shifting m_val to −₹328.99 and losing ₹24.14/qtl test mean (₹475.36 -> ₹451.22).
  3. Zero-Parameter Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 and Safe_EV_Phys_m0 Improve ES10 Without Any Tuning (Table 4): Replacing tuned kappa = 5.0 with p_dow weekday reliability and adaptive price-drop protection 1 - cv28 (where the < 2-observation 0.05 cv28 fallback touches only 86 / 37,122 = 0.23% of dispatched rows), Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 (0 free params) strengthens ES10 to −₹344.09/qtl (+₹181.17/qtl over B2_age_matched, p_holm_2s = 0.0024 at R = 5,000 across all 3 clusterings), reduces episode loss incidence to 14.93% (−11.79 pp, p_holm_2s = 0.0024), raises mean net gain by +₹32.03/qtl (₹465.59), and lowers losing-trip severity below every baseline (loss_given_loss −₹260.05 vs −₹293.73 B2 / −₹308.18 RR). The settlement-consistent variant Safe_EV_Phys_m0 (1.5F, 0 tuned params) further strengthens ES10 to −₹333.57/qtl (+₹191.69/qtl over B2, p_holm_2s = 0.0024) and lowers episode losses to 13.73%. At equal validation-matched 70.90% dispatch, Safe_EV_Sunk_matched beats RR_Abstain_matched by +₹94.31/qtl on ES10 (p_holm_2s = 0.0024..0.0040).
  4. Class-8 Phone-Calculator RT_2F_Min_m0 Leads on Mean Without cv28 or Spoilage: Removing both volatility cv28 and NABCONS spoilage leaves p_min * G > 2F, attaining ₹478.38/qtl mean (+₹44.82/qtl vs B2_age_matched, p_holm_2s = 0.0024 across all 3 clusterings—ahead of tuned RR_Abstain_matched ₹475.36) and 16.26% episode loss.
  5. Fair Feature, Volatility, and Equal-Test-Dispatch Controls (Table 5 & Figure 2): Against B2 constrained to identical test dispatch (63.27%) (ES10 −₹500.75, ep_loss 23.27%), Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 still improves ES10 by +₹156.66/qtl and lowers losses by −8.34 pp, ruling out coverage-drift explanations. Relative to a static 10% haircut (Safe_EV_fixed10pct_m0, ES10 −₹444.75), adaptive 1 - cv28 contributes +₹100.66/qtl ES10. Substituting 1.20 * euclid_km shifts Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 mean by just −₹0.39 (₹465.20), and adding 2024 climatology shifts mean by −₹2.93 (₹462.66, ES10 −₹335.36).

Still, 41.38% of dispatched HP apple trips lose money (−₹1,454.86 tail), underscoring that high-variance graded apples require live buyer confirmation prior to truck loading.

4.4 Revision v6 Robustness: Fresh 2024-Only 171-Market Rebuild, Realized ERA5 Settlement, Exact Break-Even, and 1w/4w Block Checks

To address four deeper referee concerns directly on committed files (revision/eval_v6.py, v6_upgrades.csv, v6_breakeven.csv, v6_bootstrap_5000.csv), Table 7 reports:

  1. Fresh End-to-End 2024-Only 171-Market Rebuild (N = 57,634 test episodes, 195,421 shortlisted rows, 166 clusters): Selecting eligible markets exclusively from 2024 records (>= 80 days, <= 30/state -> GJ 30, HP 23, KA 28, MP 30, MH 30, UP 30), rebuilding Top-5 lagged shortlists from scratch on those 171 raw markets (avoiding any post-hoc Top-5 truncation), and re-calibrating B2 and matched comparators strictly on val_171 (tune_threshold_on_val keeps th_b2 = ₹200.00) eliminates any post-2024 market-inclusion lookahead. Results remain virtually unchanged: Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 improves ES10 by +₹179.24/qtl under 20°C (p_holm_2s = 0.0024; H_V6_4 0.0024–0.0032; H_V6_6 Mean +₹33.12, p_holm_2s = 0.0032 origin / 0.0408 B2-dest) and by +₹187.80/qtl under realized ERA5 (Safe_EV_Phys_m0 +₹199.07/qtl, p_holm_2s = 0.0024; H_V6_6 Mean +₹34.55, p_holm_2s = 0.0024 origin / 0.0320 B2-dest).
  2. Realized ERA5 Destination Arrival-Day Weather Settlement (100.0% coordinate-day coverage across d0..d2, zero weather in decisions): Scoring the identical weather-free <= t - 1 policies against realized destination arrival-day heat, humidity, and heavy rain (>= 35 mm price-to-min compression and +0.02 rot penalty) lowers raw payoffs across every rule by ₹13–19/qtl while widening the zero-parameter advantage: on 178 markets, Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 gains +₹190.43/qtl ES10 (−₹364.28 vs −₹554.71, p_holm_2s = 0.0024), Safe_EV_Phys_m0 gains +₹201.55/qtl ES10 (−₹353.16), and RT_2F_Min_m0 leads mean at ₹464.36/qtl (+₹45.35, p_holm_2s = 0.0024). Under realized ERA5 Open-Yard MAR (which replaces no_comm_divert_d0..d2 with day-0 lagged sales at realized d0 weather and zero detention), B2 retains +₹100.57/qtl higher mean (₹707.04 vs ₹606.48 rounded), while Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 narrows ES10 by +₹196.38/qtl (−₹205.73 vs −₹402.11).
  3. Algebraically Exact Silent-Market Break-Even Thresholds (16 rows, verification_resid = 0.0): Because Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 encounters silent arrival yards (no_comm_divert) on 10.41% of episodes versus 20.16% for B2_age_matched, we compute three distinct homogeneous break-even counterfactuals where mean payoffs equalize: (a) Uniform shift above each policy's closed-yard turn-back: B2 overtakes Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 on mean only if silent trips average +₹328.37/qtl above closed-yard turn-back (+₹343.84 under ERA5; +₹348.61 on rebuilt 171-mkt 20°C; +₹363.74 on 171-mkt ERA5); (b) Separate flat constant-payoff counterfactual setting both policies' silent trips to an identical net profit above local (removing Safe_EV's shorter-corridor lower turn-back loss): +₹95.97/qtl (+₹97.25 ERA5; +₹117.97 171-mkt 20°C; +₹119.16 171-mkt ERA5); and (c) Homogeneous Open-MAR mixture share θ*: 23.79% (25.01% ERA5; 25.45% 171-mkt 20°C; 26.65% 171-mkt ERA5) of silent yards clearing at full lagged prices. For RT_2F_Min_m0 vs B2, uniform shift break-even is +₹427.54/qtl (flat constant payoff +₹186.84/qtl; 32.77% MAR share; +₹438.73 / 34.45% on 171-mkt ERA5).
  4. Calendar Block-Length Sensitivity (R = 5,000): Across 1-week (45 blocks), 2-week (23 blocks), and 4-week (12 blocks—noted as a small-cluster temporal sensitivity check) resamplings, every contrast H_V6_1..H_V6_6 remains statistically significant (p_holm_2s = 0.0024 for all tail/loss/RT-mean tests; Safe_EV mean p_holm_2s = 0.0024 [1w], 0.0028 [2w], 0.0040 [4w]).

Part 3: Related Work (49 Citations), Limitations, Novelty Overlap & Viva Defense Bank

5. Related Work and Surviving Applied Contribution

Five research streams frame our audit and design choices:

  1. Spatial Arbitrage, Market Power, and Agricultural Information Services: Parity-bound models show that gross spreads below transfer costs yield zero arbitrage [baulch1997transfer], and empirical studies of Indian wholesale integration document persistent spatial wedges driven by transport frictions, market density, and local intermediary power [sekhar2012agricultural, chatterjee2016six, negi2018farmers, mahajan2021covid, chatterjee2023market]. While mobile price discovery reduced fish waste in Kerala [jensen2007digital] and raised soybean prices near hubs [goyal2010information], randomized SMS and market-information trials show muted or heterogeneous gains when bargaining power, credit ties, or execution frictions bind [fafchamps2012sms, courtois2015farmer, mitra2018asymmetric], whereas unified e-auction platforms raise realized prices when transaction execution is reliable [levi2020impact, levi2025improving].
  2. Agricultural Price Forecasting and Market Intelligence Systems: Applied computing systems predict wholesale mandi prices via time-series, collaborative filtering, or deep learning [madaan2019price, ma2019price, guo2020mandi], study farmer-facing market intelligence workflows [ziegler2019fresh, ladhar2023ai], or reconstruct missing portal rows using regional factor models [deka2026missing]. Those studies optimize price-prediction RMSE or imputation error rather than evaluating sequential non-reporting arrival execution and worst-decile dispatch shortfall under strict <= t - 1 timing.
  3. Decision-Focused Learning and Selective Abstention: Decision-focused learning and smart predict-then-optimize frameworks align scoring directly with downstream operational loss [ban2019bigdata, elmachtoub2022smart, mandi2024dfl], while reject-option and selective-prediction theory formalizes abstention under asymmetric error costs [chow1970optimum, el_yaniv2010selective, geifman2017selective, franc2023optimal]. Our contribution demonstrates empirically that in thin agricultural portals, simple zero-parameter expected-value ratios using weekday reporting reliability and historical volatility outperform both hard activity thresholds and grid-tuned abstention penalties.
  4. Missing-Data Mechanisms, Partial Identification, and Tail Risk: Rubin's missing-data taxonomy [rubin1976inference], Manski's nonparametric bounds [manski1990bounds, horowitz2000nonparametric], selective-label evaluation [lakkaraju2017selective], and minimax policy learning under unobserved confounding [kallus2021minimax] motivate bracketing unobserved blank arrival rows rather than treating missingness as purely closed or purely open. Tail risk is measured via coherent expected shortfall [rockafellar2000cvar].
  5. Conformal Risk Control and Non-Exchangeable Inference: Distribution-free conformal prediction, risk control, and conformal decision theory [angelopoulos2023conformal, barber2023beyond, jin2023selection, angelopoulos2024conformal, lekeufack2024conformal] offer finite-sample guarantees under exchangeability or bounded shift, but fail to hold out of the box under action-dependent selective arrival denominators and correlated commodity regimes—explaining why we claim zero conformal guarantees and evaluate via two-way cluster bootstraps with finite-sample Holm corrections [phipson2010permutation, holm1979simple].

Minimal Surviving Applied Contribution: Claiming no new mathematical theorem or neural architecture, this study establishes in a strictly <= t - 1, sequentially settled retrospective audit (N = 58,676, corroborated on a fresh N = 57,634 2024-only market rebuild, realized ERA5 destination arrival-weather settlement, and N = 88,014 unconditional origins) that replacing black-box trees, hard activity cutoffs, and tuned penalties with zero-hyperparameter expected-value ratios—Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 (pdow G1SD > F), settlement-matched Safe_EV_Phys_m0 (1.5F), and Class-8 RT_2F_Min_m0 (pmin G > 2F)—eliminates tuning parameters while improving worst-10% ES10 over equal-age road dispatch (B2_age_matched) by +₹179.24 to +₹201.55/qtl across the four closed-yard panels (p_holm_2s = 0.0024 at R = 5,000), with positive 95% ES10 CIs vs B2 in every state and crop. Against tuned RR_Abstain_matched, validation-matched Safe_EV_Sunk_matched improves ES10 by +₹94.31/qtl (p_holm_2s = 0.0024–0.0040, while threshold-free Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 gains +₹116.63/qtl overall at lower 63.27% vs 69.02% coverage, trails RR by −₹9.77/qtl on aggregate mean, and trails RR by −₹16.60/qtl on Potato ES10: −₹243.97 vs −₹227.37).

6. Explicit Limitations and Non-Claims

Eight explicit boundaries govern interpretation and deployment:

  1. Modeled Payoffs ≠ Farmer Cash Income: AGMARKNET records contain no physical truck freight receipts, weighment shrinkage, or auction patti slips; freight, loading (₹35), detention (₹25), and Q10 decay are survey-anchored approximations (NITI Aayog, NABCONS, GoHP), not audited household income.
  2. A Missing Portal Quote ≠ A Physically Closed Yard: Blank arrival rows mean no public record was uploaded, not necessarily a locked gate. Under the upper Open-MAR counterfactual, B2 earns +₹102.58/qtl (+₹100.57 under ERA5) higher mean than Safe_EV_Sunk_m0, with exact break-even occurring when silent trips average +₹328.37/qtl above turn-back (23.79% Open-MAR share); even at Open-MAR, Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 retains +₹190.00/qtl (+₹196.38 ERA5) ES10 protection and lower episode losses.
  3. Alert-Triage Scope Prior to Live Phone Confirmation: Because a 30-second phone call to a destination arhtiya resolves yard closure before loading—leaving pure open-market price risk where B2 and Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 yield close open-auction means (₹930.65 vs ₹924.65) while Safe_EV halves open ES10 (−₹307.70 vs −₹623.62)—these rules serve as an upstream 6 a.m. alert filter, never a replacement for trader verification.
  4. Exploratory Calendar Exposure (Gate J = BLOCKED): Bulk AGMARKNET archives stop at 2026-04-13 (live endpoints expose only rolling 7-day snapshots), so PREREG_A10.md and PREREG_A18.md are locked exploratory follow-up protocols on a previously exposed 2025–2026 calendar, not prospective clinical-style trials.
  5. Day-t Origin Conditioning Disclosed: Primary tables condition on day-t origin uploads (58,676 of 88,014 unconditional shortlisted test episodes); full unconditional origin results (Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 ES10 −₹335.04 vs −₹515.93) confirm qualitative invariance.
  6. Residual Graded-Apple and Tomato Volatility: Although Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 narrows HP graded-apple ES10 from −₹2,392.12 to −₹1,454.86, 41.38% of dispatched apple trips still lose money; on Tomato, Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 leaves mean flat (₹461.42 vs ₹462.27) while improving ES10 by +₹195.65/qtl.
  7. District Centroids, Conflicting Duplicates, and Partial Equilibrium: 41.71% of shortlisted test rows touch district-centroid coordinates and 1,819 of 58,676 test episodes (3,096 of 95,074 combined validation and test episodes) touch conflicting duplicate records (verified stable on exact-geocode N = 40,690 and non-conflicting N = 56,857 test subsets); mass simultaneous FPO dispatch could also move thin destination prices, an equilibrium effect not modeled here.
  8. Zero-Parameter Rules ≠ Conformal Coverage Guarantees: No distribution-free coverage guarantee is claimed (Stage I H2 remained inconclusive at +₹6.13/qtl, p_holm = 0.2699).

7. Conclusion

Attractive online mandi price spreads lose money nearly half the time (45.21%) under a strict <= t - 1 chronological firewall and non-anticipative sequential arrival settlement. Stripping away black-box tree pickles, weather leakage, conformal overclaims, and tuned penalty grids leaves three zero-hyperparameter expected-value rules—Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 (pdow G1SD > F), Safe_EV_Phys_m0 (1.5F), and Class-8 RT_2F_Min_m0 (pmin G > 2F)—that any FPO coordinator can compute on a pocket calculator. Across N = 58,676 test episodes, a fresh N = 57,634 2024-only market rebuild, and realized ERA5 destination arrival-weather settlement, these rules improve worst-10% ES10 over B2_age_matched by +₹179.24 to +₹201.55/qtl (p_holm_2s = 0.0024 at R = 5,000), corroborated by +₹180.89/qtl on the N = 88,014 unconditional origin panel and strictly positive R = 1,000 95% ES10 CIs vs B2 across all six states and all five crop slices—providing an auditable, transparently bounded triage benchmark ready for prospective FPO field testing.

8. Data, Code, Reproducibility, and Ethics Statement

All analyses use strictly public, aggregated government market quotations (AGMARKNET, Open Government Data NDSAP license), public road geometry (OpenStreetMap/OSRM, ODbL), and public climate reanalysis (Copernicus ERA5, CC-BY), with zero personally identifiable farmer or trader records. Every table, figure, statistical test, and manuscript claim reproduces deterministically from tracked repository files via a single command (make reproduce), independently verified by clean-clone reproduction (0.0 maximum absolute numeric discrepancy across all CSV tables), scripts/a16_independent_audit.py (₹0.00 parity), scripts/verify_traceability.py (0 untraceable numbers across all 23 active project documents), and automated leakage tests (pytest). Because retrospective modeled payoffs do not replace real-world market discovery, deployment should be framed strictly as an informational triage aid paired with direct trader confirmation rather than autonomous truck routing.

3. Single Defensible Novelty Sentence (Surviving A12 + A17 + A18 + A20)

"Claiming no new mathematical theorem or ML architecture, this study establishes—across 58,676 strictly causal (<= t - 1), sequentially settled wholesale dispatch episodes, a fresh 2024-only 171-market panel (N = 57,634), realized ERA5 destination arrival-weather settlement, and an 88,014-episode unconditional origin audit across six states and four crops—that replacing black-box trees, hard activity gates, and tuned penalty grids with zero-hyperparameter expected-value rules (Safe_EV_Sunk_m0, settlement-matched Safe_EV_Phys_m0, and Class-8 RT_2F_Min_m0) improves worst-10% shortfall by +₹181.17 to +₹201.55/qtl over equal-age road dispatch (p_holm_2s = 0.0024 at R = 5,000 across all three clusterings and 1-, 2-, 4-week blocks) and by +₹94.31/qtl at validation-matched dispatch over tuned RR-Abstain (p_holm_2s = 0.0024..0.0040, noting Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 trails RR by −₹16.60 on Potato ES10), with positive 95% ES10 CIs vs B2 across all six states and all five crop slices, all 36 tornado cells, exact-zero diversion (+₹169.79), and graded apples (−₹1,454.86 vs −₹2,392.12) as a transparent upstream 6 a.m. alert filter prior to trader confirmation—while openly disclosing its exploratory calendar boundary (Gate J), exact silent-market break-even (+₹328.37/qtl above turn-back; 23.79% Open-MAR share), and Open-MAR mean reversal (B2 +₹102.58)."

(All numbers verified strictly from revision/results/, reproduced cleanly via make reproduce, zero untraceable numbers (scripts/verify_traceability.py), independent A16 match within ₹0.00 across all 8 policies, R = 5,000 paired cluster bootstrap across all 3 State| clusterings and 1-, 2-, 4-week blocks.)

Q1. What is the single problem and why did naive portal arbitrage fail so often?

An online AGMARKNET spread looks like instant profit (> ₹100/qtl), yet across 58,676 lagged test episodes (2025-06-01..2026-04-08), blindly chasing top spreads (B1_lagged_screen, 100.00% dispatch) loses money on 45.21% of days (mean ₹397.87/qtl, exact ES10 −₹641.26/qtl). Three physical frictions—road freight (₹35 + 0.45 * hp * km), destination post-spoilage APMC seller fees (0.5%–1.5%), and 28.98% (17,005 trips) encountering zero uploaded trade on arrival—turn paper spreads into turn-back losses under sequential non-anticipative settlement.

Q2. Why did you move beyond tuned RR-Abstain (kappa*=5.0) to zero-parameter Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 & RT_2F_Min_m0?

Adversarial review (A17 + A18) uncovered three clean flaws in RR-Abstain:

  1. kappa* = 5.0 hit the grid wall: Extending the grid to 20.0 pushed the matched threshold down to −₹328.99/qtl (showing kappa = 5.0 worked as a disguised cutoff shift rather than a physical 1.5× return factor).
  2. rep28 over-predicted Sunday closings: Mandis closed regularly on Sundays still scored 0.75 under a 28-day rolling average, inflating 0.5*rep28 + 0.5*dow8. Using weekday-only dow8 ((k+1)/10 over the last 8 same-weekdays) fixed Sunday prediction directly.
  3. Price swings (cv28) were ignored: High lagged prices regress downward on arrival (Apple / Tomato). Subtracting 1 standard deviation (dest_price_cv_28d) gives Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 (pdow· G1SD - F > 0 — 0 free params, cuts ES10 from −₹525.25 to −₹344.09/qtl, +₹181.17 vs B2, p_holm_2s = 0.0024 at R = 5,000 on all 3 clustering schemes and 1-, 2-, 4-week blocks; Mean +₹32.03, p_holm_2s = 0.0028–0.0436; positive ES10 vs B2 in all 6 states and HP apples). Dropping cv28 altogether leaves Class-8 RT_2F_Min_m0 (pmin· G > 2F — 0 free params, ₹478.38/qtl mean, +₹44.82 vs B2, p_holm_2s = 0.0024).

Q3. Why would an FPO use your math instead of just calling a trader on the phone (A17 #10)?

It doesn't replace the phone call—it prevents alert overload before the call. A manager gets dozens of noisy AGMARKNET spreads every morning across 30+ yards; Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 and RT_2F_Min_m0 filter out sporadic Sunday-closed and hyper-volatile traps in milliseconds before the FPO calls destination arhtiyas to confirm live auctions. Moreover, even on pure realized open auctions (exact_d0 trips only, where trader calls confirm openings), Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 cuts ES10 tail risk in half (−₹307.70 vs B2 −₹623.62) while nearly matching open mean (₹924.65 vs ₹930.65, unlike tuned RR which lost −₹94.44).

Q4. Explain exact ES10 and what cluster-key bug your own adversarial review caught (A17 #1).

Unweighted below-quantile averages (the legacy truncated quantile-mean estimator) broke whenever ₹0 abstentions tied at the 10% boundary. Exact ES10 sorts all N episodes worst-first (₹0 on abstentions), sets fractional mass m = 0.10 N = k + f, sums the worst k observations plus fraction f of (k + 1), and divides by m. On clustering: earlier runs forgot State + "|" on bare dest_market, splitting physical markets into 336 duplicate strings instead of 172. Fixing State + "|" and adding policy-specific destination clustering yields exact 173, 172, and 171–173 clusters (1-week 45, 2-week 23, and 4-week 12 calendar blocks) and uses strict two-sided Holm-Bonferroni at R = 5,000 (p_holm_2s = 0.0024 for tail/loss/RT-mean; 0.0028–0.0436 for Safe_EV mean vs B2)—all primary hypotheses still hold cleanly across all 3 schemes.

Q5. Isn't every gain just an artifact of penalizing blank AGMARKNET rows as return trips (div = 1.5)?

We directly tested five stronger sensitivity regimes (a18_missing_regimes.csv):

  • Even at div_0.0_spoil_only (where RR's ES10 diff collapsed to NS +₹9.81, p_2s = 0.603), Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 STILL beats B2 by +₹173.65/qtl ES10 (−₹185.52 vs −₹359.17, p_2s = 0.002)!
  • Even at literal zero diversion payoff (exact_zero_divert_payoff_0, payoff ₹0 on blank arrival), Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 beats B2 by +₹169.79/qtl ES10 (p_2s = 0.002) and cuts episode losses (4.52% vs 6.55%).
  • Only under upper-bound open_yard_MAR_lagged_price (pretending 100% of blank portal rows actually cleared open at yesterday's price) does B2 beat Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 on Mean (₹722.66 vs ₹620.08; ₹707.04 vs ₹606.48 under realized ERA5)—yet Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 STILL reduces losses (4.78% vs 7.08%) and beats B2 on ES10 (+₹190.00 at 20°C; +₹196.38 under ERA5). Moreover, exact algebraic break-even (v6_breakeven.csv, residual 0.0) shows B2 catches Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 on Mean only if silent yards average +₹328.37/qtl uniform shift above turn-back (or +₹95.97/qtl under a separate flat constant-payoff counterfactual where every silent trip yields one constant value, or 23.79% homogeneous Open-MAR share; +₹363.74 / +₹119.16 / 26.65% on the fresh 171-market ERA5 rebuild), and RT_2F_Min_m0 break-even requires +₹427.54/qtl (+₹186.84 flat constant payoff; 32.77% MAR share). That directly exposes exact boundaries without hiding anything!

Q6. Wait—didn't building episodes only on days when the origin reported on day t leak sample selection (A17 #4)?

Yes, and we explicitly audit and test it! Conditioning primary episodes on settle_local_price_d0 dropped 29,338 of 88,014 unconditional test episodes where the origin mandi failed to publish on day t. When we rebuild the full unconditional N = 88,014 panel (a18_settlement_and_robustness.csv), Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 performs even better: Mean ₹483.03 vs B2 ₹445.37, EpLoss 15.22% vs 28.10%, and ES10 −₹335.04 vs −₹515.93 (while RT_2F_Min_m0 reaches ₹493.15 mean). Results also hold identically across origin_lag_age 1..3 (N = 56,648), exact-geocoded corridors (N = 40,690, excluding the 41.71% rows touching district centroids), and non-conflicting duplicate keys (N = 56,857).

Q7. How does Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 perform across all 6 states, all crops, and HP Graded Apples (R6)?

  • All 6 States (100% pass vs RR failing MH/HP): Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 earns strictly positive 95% ES10 CIs in Gujarat [+₹138.05, +₹369.11], HP [+₹59.18, +₹637.28], Karnataka [+₹58.23, +₹184.08], MP [+₹139.94, +₹303.97], Maharashtra [+₹48.71, +₹303.07], and UP [+₹48.00, +₹139.86].
  • Crops (a18_crop_and_state_splits.csv): Gains ES10 vs B2_age_matched on Non-Apple (+₹135.58), Onion (+₹123.49), Potato (+₹72.31 vs B2, while transparently trailing RR_Abstain_matched on Potato ES10 by −₹16.60: −₹243.97 vs −₹227.37), Tomato (+₹195.65), and generic Apple (+₹561.37). Transparently, Safe_EV_Sunk_m0's Mean net-gain CIs vs B2 cross zero in Gujarat (−₹1.66), Maharashtra ([−₹5.58, +₹36.32]), UP ([−₹3.18, +₹27.00]), Tomato (₹461.42 vs ₹462.27), and Apple ([−₹24.81, +₹245.04]) due to conservative risk filtering (cnt28 < 2 fallback hits just 0.23% / 86 dispatched rows), whereas zero-parameter RT_2F_Min_m0 beats B2's point Mean in all 6 states and all 5 crop slices (Tomato ₹504.35).
  • HP Graded Apples (N = 2,802, a18_hp_apple.csv): Previously MG_matched beat RR on ES10 (−₹1,953.20 vs −₹2,165.73). Zero-parameter Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 beats both: Mean ₹1,354.85 (vs B2 ₹1,199.31, MG ₹1,028.05), ES10 −₹1,454.86 (−₹2,479.28 vs B2 −₹4,071.95 in June–Aug 2026). Still, 41.38% of dispatched HP apple trips lose money, so live buyer checks remain mandatory (R6).

Q8. What if transport is heavy-truck (₹0.258/km), arhtiya commission is 6%, market selection uses 2024-only data, or realized ERA5 arrival weather affects spoilage (A8, N1, v6)?

  • Weather leak cleanly removed from decisions (N1) & Realized ERA5 Settlement (v6): Forecast rain matched ERA5 rain on 66,222 / 67,135 (98.64%) rows; zero weather enters any decision rule. Primary tables use 20°C NABCONS reference (2024 climatology shifts Safe_EV ES10 to −₹335.36). Settling the identical weather-free rules against 100.0%-covered realized arrival-day ERA5 temperature (Q10), RH, and heavy rain (>= 35 mm) widens Safe_EV_Sunk_m0's ES10 advantage to +₹190.43/qtl (−₹364.28 vs −₹554.71; Safe_EV_Phys_m0 +₹201.55/qtl, p_holm_2s = 0.0024 at R = 5,000).
  • Fresh End-to-End Rebuilt Strict 2024-Only 171-Market Zero-Lookahead Panel (N = 57,634): Selecting markets exclusively on 2024 reporting days (>= 80 days, <= 30/state), freshly rebuilding Top-5 candidates from 171 markets (195,421 shortlisted test rows), and re-calibrating B2 on val_171 (th = ₹200) preserves every conclusion (Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 +₹179.24 ES10 at 20°C, +₹187.80 under realized ERA5; Safe_EV_Phys_m0 +₹199.07; p_holm_2s = 0.0024 across 1-, 2-, and 4-week calendar blocks).
  • 36-of-36 Tornado Robustness (a18_tornado.csv): Across all 18 freight (₹0.258 NITI floor to ₹1.20 steep), arhtiya (0–6%), HP hill (1.0–1.75), spoilage (0.5–2x), and detention (₹0–100) checks under BOTH frozen and re-scored decisions, Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 beats B2_age_matched in 36 of 36 scenarios on Mean (+₹13.31..+₹61.11) AND ES10 (+₹144.94..+₹329.37) with zero sign flips!
